<PAGE><|det|>header [55, 77, 308, 116]<|/det|>8. Findings
<|det|>title [105, 151, 525, 188]<|/det|>8.1. Critical Findings
<|det|>title [105, 223, 940, 298]<|/det|>[C-01] Incorrect parenthesis usage results in a completely wrong calculation
<|det|>title [105, 321, 250, 352]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [136, 364, 287, 386]<|/det|>Impact: High
<|det|>text [136, 404, 325, 425]<|/det|>Likelihood: High
<|det|>title [105, 445, 307, 475]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [135, 488, 913, 533]<|/det|>Upon calling Edge.calcLowerImplied() when the price is below the narrow range low tick, we have the following piece of code:
<|det|>text [149, 559, 517, 575]<|/det|>uint256 xyX192 = (x << (128 / y)) << 64;
<|det|>text [134, 604, 940, 740]<|/det|>It aims to compute the x/y ratio in 192-bit precision by first moving x to 128-bit precision, dividing by y and then going to 192-bit precision when shifting left by 64 bits. However, the formula has a critical issue as x is shifted left by 128 / y bits due to the parenthesis usage, this will round down to 0 in pretty much every case which results in the variable simply holding the value of x shifted left by 64 bits.
<|det|>text [135, 759, 644, 779]<|/det|>This vulnerability is also in a few other functions.
<|det|>title [105, 801, 423, 827]<|/det|>Recommendations
<|det|>text [145, 849, 534, 879]<|/det|>+ uint256 xyx192 = ((x << 128) / y) << 64;
- uint256 xyx192 = (x << (128 / y)) << 64;
<|det|>page_number [491, 963, 508, 979]<|/det|>9
